solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flower arrangement's last bloom, good for bedding

indicators.note: the word last asks for the final letter of the word arrangement

parts.note: the word arrangement itself, its letters to be picked from

indicators.note: good is put to bed inside the flower, tucked in among its letters

parts.note: an iris is a garden bloom

explanation.surface: A florist's note: the last bloom in the arrangement is a good one for planting out in a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as something that flows, a river, not a bloom. 'For bedding' puts G inside IRIS to make IGRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention reads flower as a thing that flows; the Tigris is a great river of Iraq.

clue.text: Officer sorting out spat in petty quarrel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the quarrel

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble

indicators.note: sorting letters puts them into a new order, rearranging spat

explanation.surface: A police officer resolves a minor dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spat' itself means a quarrel, a tempting synonym for the outer piece, but here it is the fodder that 'sorting out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer, historically one carrying a metal-tipped staff of office.

clue.text: First of generals a licentious one, revered nationalist

indicators.note: First of asks for the opening letter of generals

parts.note: ribald means coarse and licentious
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A leading general was a womaniser yet still a beloved patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Garibaldi was a general himself, fitting the surface; in Britain his name is also on a currant biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi led the fight for Italian unification and is a national hero in Italy.

clue.text: Foot — British leader introducing himself?

parts.note: a man introducing himself says I am

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, here of British

explanation.surface: A British prime minister stands up and introduces himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is the poetic unit, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse, a metrical foot is a unit of stressed and unstressed syllables; the iamb is short then long.

clue.text: Irritable bowels of Fräulein nursed by favourite soldier?

indicators.note: being nursed by someone means being held in their arms, so these letters sit inside the others

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
a soldier ant is a kind of ant; the question mark flags the insect sense

indicators.note: bowels are the innermost parts, so take the central letters of the German word

explanation.surface: A young German woman with an upset stomach is being cared for by a beloved soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowels of' takes the central pair of letters of the eight-letter German word; 'soldier?' points to the soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone petulant is sulky and bad-tempered, quick to take offence like a cross child.

clue.text: Old Italian cars, ten taking a spin around Umbria, primarily

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the single letter
spinning letters round mixes them up, so cars and ten are rearranged
primarily gives the first letter of Umbria

explanation.surface: Ten cars go for a drive around the Italian region of Umbria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a spin' rearranges CARS TEN to ETRSCAN, which goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were an ancient people of central Italy, before Rome took over.

clue.text: Happy with position, honest!

parts.note: up means cheerful, in high spirits
standing is one's position or status

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased with their job, honestly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honest!' looks like an exclamation of sincerity but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an upstanding person is respectable and of good character, morally upright.

clue.text: A second way to be taken when shocked?

definitions.text: way to be taken when shocked?

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: A second road option for a startled traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a unit of time or an ordinal but is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken aback means being startled, so this is the manner in which a startled person is taken.

clue.text: Final bit parts go in

indicators.note: the final bit parts the other word, splitting it open to sit inside

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
the end is the final bit

explanation.surface: An actor's last small roles start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit parts' looks like small acting roles, but 'parts' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable, as in the in thing; trendy means stylish and up to date.

clue.text: Pop over about one? I'm off!

indicators.note: the reversed drink goes about the single letter, surrounding it
over turns the drink over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: pop is a fizzy drink, soda
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dad pops round for one and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like father or a visit, but is a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Adios is Spanish for goodbye, a parting phrase like I'm leaving now.

clue.text: Solid girl blocking sink, pulled from the rear

indicators.note: pulling something out from its back end reads it backwards, last letter first
the girl's name sits inside the word for sink, blocking it

parts.note: to dip is to sink or drop briefly
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl has clogged the sink and some solid lump has to be dragged out from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' is the geometric noun, not an adjective; 'pulled from the rear' reverses the whole assembly, giving DIMARYP read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a pyramid is a solid figure with a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at a point.

clue.text: Once again mould turn of phrase, English

indicators.note: a turn of the letters gives them a new order, so the word phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone revises their writing, recasting an English turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of phrase' looks like an idiom but 'turn of' rearranges PHRASE into RESHAP, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix re- means again, and to shape is to mould, so the verb means form anew.

clue.text: Pipe travelling underground, bewilderingly expensive for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so take the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Riding London's Underground, the Tube, is baffling and costs a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a tube is a hollow cylinder through which liquid or gas passes, much like a pipe.

clue.text: Surprised when teeth knocked out, say?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a punch to the mouth (British slang gob) that could knock out teeth

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked after a punch knocks their teeth out.
explanation.walkthrough: Gob is British slang for mouth, so the British word for astonished can be read as a literal blow to the face.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for astonished, as though struck in the mouth by the news.

clue.text: Oscar winner receiving prize, ultimately, for African native

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright

indicators.note: the winner takes in the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them, so best stands in for winning

indicators.note: ultimately gives the final letter of prize

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winning actor finally collects a prize for playing an African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar winner' looks like a film award, but Oscar is Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is an antelope found wild on the plains of Africa.

clue.text: Back medicine providing pick- me-up

indicators.note: taking things back reads them in reverse, so the two words run right to left

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine
if means providing that, on condition that

explanation.surface: Medicine for a bad back gives you a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like the body part but signals reading PILLIF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a fillip is a stimulus or boost that lifts the spirits, like a tonic.

clue.text: Field that's flat, cut

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or apartment
to dock is to cut short, as with a tail or wages

explanation.surface: A farmer describes a field that is level and mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an adjective describing the field but is the noun for a home, PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field, especially one for horses.

clue.text: Get down from there? You're kidding!

definitions.meaning: a call to dismount from something
an exclamation of disbelief at someone's claim

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means climb down; as an idiom it is a scornful cry of disbelief.

clue.text: Idiot feeding burrowing animals syrup

indicators.note: the idiot is fed into the animals, going inside them

parts.note: moles are small burrowing mammals
an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A fool is feeding syrup to moles.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: molasses is the thick dark syrup left after refining sugar, the American word for treacle.

clue.text: Goodness in fish that's deceptive

indicators.note: the exclamation goes inside the word for fish

parts.note: fry are young fish
lumme is an old British exclamation of surprise, like goodness me

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a fish that is misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: Lumme, or lummy, is a dated Cockney cry of surprise, from Lord love me.
explanation.definitionFit: Flummery is empty flattery or humbug, talk that is meant to deceive, as well as a soft pudding.

clue.text: House turned gold

parts.note: winds means turns, as a road winds round a hill, taken here as the past-tense idea of turning
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A building has been painted or gilded gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The British royal family took the name of the House of Windsor in 1917, turning from Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, which the surface may hint at.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is the name of the reigning British royal house, a dynasty rather than a building.

clue.text: Being eaten by human, I'm alarmed

indicators.note: the word sits inside these clue words as if swallowed by them

explanation.surface: A frightened creature cries out on being eaten by a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a living creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an animal is a living creature, a being, as opposed to a plant or object.

clue.text: Scorer and cutter

definitions.meaning: the American composer Samuel ..., who wrote scores

explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Barber composed the Adagio for Strings; a barber is also a men's hairdresser.

clue.text: In the end, you learned operation

indicators.note: In the end gives the final letter of you

parts.note: sage means wise and learned

explanation.surface: Eventually you came to understand how it works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' looks like the verb but is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: usage is the way something is used or operated, its employment.

clue.text: Jiggling of large bits beyond a student of valued relationships?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after, lying beyond, the single letter
jiggling shakes things about, so the letters of large bits are rearranged

explanation.surface: Large pieces of something are being shaken past a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jiggling of' rearranges LARGE BITS into LGEBRAIST, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An algebraist studies equations, relationships between values, punned as relationships people value.

clue.text: Pot badger upended before bottom ripped from vessel

indicators.note: the turned word comes before the trimmed vessel
upending a word in a down clue turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to badger is to nag

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, so the final letter is torn off

parts.note: a jar is a vessel

explanation.surface: A badger knocks over a pot, ripping the base from a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' is cannabis, not a pan. 'Bottom ripped from' takes R off JAR to leave JA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganja is a slang name for cannabis, which is also called pot.

clue.text: Report a time of prosperity

definitions.meaning: a loud bang, like the report of a gun
an economic upturn of rapid growth

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the loud deep noise of a gun, and a period of rapid economic growth.

clue.text: Three tenors rejoicing in operatic overtures

indicators.note: overtures are openings, so take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: The Three Tenors sing joyfully in opera overtures.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Three Tenors, the famous singing trio.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, especially of musicians.

clue.text: Fireworks in crates?

definitions.meaning: crates is slang for old, worn-out cars

explanation.surface: Fireworks are stored in boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crates' looks like boxes, but is slang for clapped-out cars; in Britain an old car is a banger, as is a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: firecrackers that explode loudly, and British slang for decrepit old cars.

clue.text: African native stripping lead from wood in error

indicators.note: the trimmed wood goes inside the word for error

parts.note: a gaffe is a blunder or social error

indicators.note: the lead letter is the first, so the opening letter is removed from the tree

parts.note: fir is a tree and a wood

explanation.surface: An African is mistakenly stripping lead from timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal but means the first letter; 'stripping lead from' trims the tree's opening letter before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is an animal native to the African savannah, the tallest living land animal.

clue.text: Check out when nuts roasted with joint, finally

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of roasted go haywire into a new order
finally points to the last letter of the word joint

explanation.surface: A roast dinner of nuts and a joint of meat is checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like food beside 'roasted' but is the anagram signal, making ROADTES from ROASTED, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: To road-test is to try out a vehicle or product in real use, checking it out before buying.

clue.text: Steep gradient, hill ends comfortable touring

indicators.note: the cosy word travels round the two end letters, enclosing them

parts.note: cosy means comfortable and snug

indicators.note: ends gives the final letters of gradient and hill

explanation.surface: A walker finds a steep gradient on a hill easy enough on a comfortable tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like a slope beside 'gradient' and 'hill', but means pricey. 'Touring' puts T and L inside COSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is an informal word for a price that is too high, expensive.
